newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market's resiliency surprises.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Market's resiliency surprises.

text.p: The U.S. stock market's resiliency Wednesday surprised options traders and brokers who expected some kind of a pullback after Tuesday's sharp rally.
"It is surprising, especially after yesterday," said one index options broker in Chicago. "I'm looking for it to possibly rally a little tomorrow but the number Friday will definitely knock it down."
The April U.S. employment report is scheduled to be released Friday before the stock market opens.
Traders said the turnaround in bond prices was the main reason stocks were able to power higher.
"I think we saw some profit-taking right out of the shoot this morning but then bonds came back a full point and I think that had a lot to do with it," one S&P 100 index .OEX options trader said.

In late trading, most market indices were in positive territory off their session highs. Most had posted early losses as bonds fell after the stronger-than-expected first quarter gross domestic product report.
GDP rose 5.6 percent compared with expectations of a 4.1 percent growth rate.
The OEX was up 6.97 points at 785.31 after climbing to 789.55. The S&P 500 index .SPX was ahead 6.71 at nearly 801. It reached an intraday high of 804.
June S&P 500 futures, after hitting 810, were up 4.90 points at 804.70.
Fair value was seen at about a 3.65-point premium to cash.
"We're looking to buy put spreads" in the OEX, the broker said, adding that put spreads appeared to be the main strategy being played out Tuesday as well.
On Tuesday, some of the biggest trades were put spreads in a couple OEX June options.
"I think there's still time, with about two-and-a-half weeks until expiration, for an attempt to knock (the market) down," he explained.
The heaviest volume in May OEX puts was in the 760 strike, where volume topped 8,000 contracts. The May 770 put traded 6,700 contracts and the May 740 put traded about 6,400.
On the call side, the May 800 traded about 8,100 contracts and the May 790 traded 7,700.
The broker said that overall, trading was relatively quiet.
"When you call the crowd, it's not real busy," he said.

The OEX trader agreed. "I just don't think that the world is really hedging," he said. "When we started to go down they were hedging, but now that we're heading back up again they've all gotten out of it and we just have people taking small shots in here but nothing major."
He added that volatility continued to hold up fairly well despite the market's rally.
"I think it's the puts not dropping as much as they should that's holding it up," he said.
